rationale: Both candidates independently and correctly identify the same central live bug that matches the ground-truth's core surviving concern: the MiniMax-H3-specific rel_l1_thresh=0.17 default never reaches the engine because _get_default_cache_config hardcodes 0.2, with matching file/line citations. X goes considerably further, verifying the partition-gating fix (matching ground-truth concern 1) is correct, then adding well-grounded, concretely actionable findings on memory retention, wasted RoPE computation, weak E2E cache-hit assertions, a cache-hit test that can't catch stale conditioning, and a drive-by frame-count change — all with specific file:line references and suggested fixes. Y is tight and precise but covers only the one issue in depth, with a brief unelaborated confirmation of other areas. X's greater breadth of grounded, actionable findings outweighs its slightly lower precision from more speculative claims (e.g., the polynomial R² analysis).
